article.title: Notorious Mexican Drug Lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo Dies at 80
article.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, the notorious Mexican drug kingpin known as 'the boss of bosses' who orchestrated the 1985 murder of U.S. DEA agent Enrique 'Kiki' Camarena, has died at age 80 from multiple organ failure.

article.content_html:
Key Developments

Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, recognized as the architect of modern Mexican drug trafficking and a founder of the Guadalajara cartel, died on November 15 at a medical facility in Jalisco, Mexico. According to the security ministry of Jalisco, the 80-year-old kingpin suffered multiple organ failure after being transferred from prison to the hospital two days earlier due to a guarded prognosis.

Felix Gallardo, a former police officer and bodyguard, had been incarcerated since 1989 and was serving a 40-year sentence. He was convicted for the 1985 kidnapping, torture, and murder of undercover U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena Salazar. In recent years, his health had severely deteriorated, with conditions including high blood pressure, diabetes, and deafness.

Key Takeaways

  • Death of a Kingpin: Felix Gallardo passed away at age 80 from multiple organ failure following a recent transfer from prison to a hospital.
  • U.S. Agent Murder: He was serving a 40-year sentence for orchestrating the 1985 assassination of undercover DEA agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena.
  • Cartel Legacy: As a founder of the Guadalajara cartel—the precursor to the Sinaloa cartel—he fundamentally transformed the global cocaine trade and forged powerful alliances with Colombian traffickers.

Why It Matters

The death of Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo marks the end of an era for the historic leadership of Mexican cartels. As "the boss of bosses," his rise shaped the modern landscape of transnational organized crime by connecting Colombian cocaine suppliers with routes into the United States. The 1985 murder of DEA agent Enrique Camarena triggered a massive geopolitical outcry from Washington, forever altering U.S.-Mexico security cooperation and law enforcement strategies targeting the drug trade.
